label: early original-phase q/y/k/2/u/w after an x/t/z/j/m-initial prefix
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase (input) unit: 99.6% of mass at t<L, none at t=0/1, peaking at t=3 (t=2-5 carry ~93% of mass). It is graded by the current input token (q, y, k, 2 strongest, then u, w, 0; about 4-5x lift each) combined with the earlier prefix, being strongest when the sequence begins with, or two steps back has, x/t/z/j/m (first_tok x has 5.2x lift). Top examples look like x x n [q], m x t t [k], x t j [y]. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of the input token (95% of mass has in_first=1). It is essentially silent at the delimiter and in the copy phase. It looks like a distributed, additive token x prefix code rather than a crisp rule: the broad predicate (original phase, t>=2, in_tok in the set) gets 81% of mass but only 11% precision, and the recorded conjunction reaches dev F1 0.40 (P 0.42, R 0.38, mass 0.48). Many lower-magnitude activations come from other tokens (g, e, h, n) or other prefixes.
